note: v18 opens 'So we fix our eyes not on what is seen' and completes the sentence begun in v17.

'our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory that is far beyond comparison.' (2Cor 4:17), beside 'our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us' (Rom 8:18). One writer, two letters, the same two things weighed against each other -- and reached differently: 2Corinthians weighs them, Romans refuses to.
'an eternal weight of glory that is far beyond comparison' (2Cor 4:17).

'what is unseen is eternal' (2Cor 4:18); 'the certainty of what we do not see' (Heb 11:1). The phrase is the same and neither writer cites the other, so the pairing is the graph's -- but the wording is not the graph's, it is theirs.

The same contrast, nine verses later in the same letter, turned from a property of things into a way of going. Paul does not refer back and the chapter break sits between them, so this is the graph's join on the terms he supplies.
'we walk by faith, not by sight' (2Cor 5:7).
